_note: Every factual claim the narration makes, with the source that carries it on screen. BRIEF.md §7: 'every claim carries its source on screen'. A claim with no source here does not go in the script.

pistons_three_years.claim: Detroit eliminated Chicago in three consecutive postseasons, 1988, 1989 and 1990 — twice in the Eastern Conference Finals.

jordan_rules.claim: Detroit's defensive scheme against him was known as the Jordan Rules — a deliberate policy of physical punishment every time he drove.

grover_approach.claim: Tim Grover approached Jordan in 1989 after reading that he was tired of taking physical abuse from the Pistons.

thirty_days.claim: Jordan agreed to a thirty-day trial. It ran for fifteen years.

fifteen_pounds.claim: By the 1990-91 season he had added about fifteen pounds of muscle.

breakfast_club.claim: The sessions began between five and seven in the morning at his Highland Park home. Scottie Pippen, Ron Harper and Randy Brown joined them. They called it the Breakfast Club.
breakfast_club.card: THE BREAKFAST CLUB · 5–7 AM · HIGHLAND PARK

lift_list.claim: The programme was built on squats, leg extensions, weighted step-ups, deadlifts, good mornings, power cleans, bench press and biceps curls.
lift_list.card: SQUAT · DEADLIFT · POWER CLEAN · STEP-UP · GOOD MORNING · BENCH

never_stopped.claim: Grover: 'I would give him a certain amount of reps to do, but he would never stop at that number. If I asked for six, I knew he was gonna do twelve.'

swept_1991.claim: In 1991 Chicago swept Detroit four games to nothing, then beat the Lakers four games to one for the first championship.

steak_four_hours.claim: His pre-game meal was steak and potato, four hours before tip-off.

against_the_orthodoxy.claim: The 1980s and 90s prescription for athletes was carbohydrate loading — rice and pasta. His plan did the opposite: the steak slowed digestion and held his blood sugar steady.
against_the_orthodoxy.card: THE ERA SAID CARBS. HE ATE STEAK.

flu_game.claim: Game 5 of the 1997 Finals: 38 points. Grover says it was not flu but food poisoning, from a pizza delivered to the team hotel in Park City.
